chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: There is no manumission for the believer after death.
And there is no will for him in one-third of his wealth, unless it is for a debt or a bequest to one of his family.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a believer's will and manumission after death in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that the manumission of a slave upon death is treated as a bequest (wasiyyah), thereby subject to the standard one-third limit of the estate after debts are settled. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between immediate transfer of ownership and posthumous bequests, ensuring that the believer's remaining obligations to heirs are not compromised. It underscores the balance between charitable emancipation and financial responsibility within the framework of Islamic inheritance law.
